item: Data in transit protection: user data crossing networks is protected against eavesdropping and tampering
repo_note: TLS minimum, HTTPS redirect, managed certificate at the edge; backend traffic not required to use TLS.

item: Physical location and legal jurisdiction: know where data is stored and processed, and which laws reach it
repo_note: No rule to record regions or every processor's jurisdiction; an ADR would fit.

item: Data centre security: sites holding data are physically protected
repo_note: Inherited from the cloud provider; cite its own statement against the principles.

item: Data encryption: data at rest is protected from anyone with physical access to the infrastructure
repo_note: Default encryption on every store; customer-managed keys for tokens and credentials. No guard test pins it.

item: Data sanitisation and equipment disposal: data is removed when it leaves the service, and media disposed of securely
repo_note: Deletion list covers stores, prefixes and backups; media disposal inherited; no per-customer key to destroy.

item: Physical resilience and availability: the service meets its availability commitments through failures
repo_note: Deletion protection and stateful-destroy review; recovery optional and paid; no restore test or stated SLA.

item: Separation between customers: one customer cannot reach or affect another's service or data
repo_note: Silo first, a non-code barrier on every deployment, isolation and barrier tests against the real store.

item: Governance framework: a framework that coordinates and directs the management of the service and its information
repo_note: Management system; the ISO 27001 checklist covers it.

item: Vulnerability management: weaknesses in the provider's components are found, prioritised and fixed
repo_note: New advisories blocked; no fix deadline for existing ones; end-of-life runtimes not retired.

item: Protective monitoring: attacks, misuse and malfunction are detected and acted on quickly
repo_note: Errors reported and firewall logs on the paid tier; no security events logged or watched.

item: Incident management: planned incident response, and customers told when their data is affected
repo_note: No runbook, owner or customer notification rule (33 §7).

item: Configuration and change management: components tracked, changes assessed, unauthorised changes caught
repo_note: Infrastructure as code, plan reviewed, pipeline-only applies, guard tests; no drift detection or account trail.

item: People and security culture: staff access limited and staff screened to suit their role
repo_note: Screening and culture; not in repo.

item: Technical controls for service administration: staff access to customer data logged, monitored and limited
repo_note: Audited operator role, one cross-tenant override, data-blind production; no alert on staff access.

item: Secure development: the service is designed, built and deployed to reduce security threats
repo_note: Threat model, gated CI, ASVS review; no SAST or secret scanning yet (33 §4).

item: Supply chain security: suppliers and their supply chains support the principles the service claims
repo_note: Software inputs controlled; no list of suppliers holding customer data, no supplier assurance.

item: Secure user management: customers get tools to control who can access the service and their data
repo_note: Role gate, tenant administrator, admin-only accounts; no time-bounded privilege or removal of unused access.

item: Identity and authentication: every access to a service interface is from a verified identity
repo_note: Managed identity, token verified at edge and gateway; MFA offered not required; no customer SSO rule.

item: External interface protection: every external or less-trusted interface is identified and defended
repo_note: Edge firewall, anonymous endpoints explicit, rate limits, signed webhooks, tool-server allowlist.

item: Secure service administration: the systems used to administer the service are highly protected
repo_note: Pipeline-only changes, federated credentials, account per environment; no MFA or admin device rule.

item: Audit information: customers get the audit records to investigate use of their service and data
repo_note: Platform audit log is internal; no customer-visible sign-in or change history.

item: Security alerts: customers are alerted promptly, through an automated channel, to attacks or compromise
repo_note: No customer security alert of any kind.

item: Security by design and by default: the service resists common attacks out of the box; customer duties are stated
repo_note: No open sign-up, required privacy flag, fail-closed route table; customer duties still to write.

item: Help customers meet their security responsibilities: visibility of their resources and settings
repo_note: No customer-facing security guide or settings view.

item: Follow an established secure development framework
repo_note: ASVS level chosen by ADR and this set; no mapping to a recognised SDLC framework.

item: Know the components in the software and assess the risk of third-party ones
repo_note: Every direct dependency a named decision; no SBOM per release (33 §4).

item: A defined test process for software and updates before release
repo_note: Gated CI, green end-to-end before release, security review triggers.

item: Secure by design and secure by default through the whole lifecycle
repo_note: Threat model kept with the code; secure defaults with guard tests.

item: Protect the build environment from unauthorised access
repo_note: Pinned actions, no install scripts, federated credentials; no MFA on the git host, no runner hardening.

item: Control and log changes to the build environment
repo_note: Workflows are code, reviewed and pinned; host and runner settings changed outside review, unlogged.

item: Distribute software to customers securely
repo_note: Pipeline deploys over TLS; mobile builds signed, keys held by the build service.

item: Have and publish a vulnerability disclosure process
repo_note: No disclosure policy or security.txt (33 §7).

item: Detect, prioritise and manage vulnerabilities in the software and its components
repo_note: Advisory gate and scheduled report; no fix deadline, no SAST.

item: Report vulnerabilities to relevant external parties where appropriate
repo_note: No rule to report upstream to a component's maintainer or to a coordinator.

item: Provide timely security updates and tell customers about them
repo_note: One deploy patches every customer; no fix deadline, no security advisory to customers.

item: Tell customers the level of support and maintenance provided
repo_note: Commercial terms; not in repo.

item: Give at least a year's notice before support for a product ends
repo_note: Commercial commitment; API versioning helps, no notice period for app builds or API versions.

item: Share information with customers about notable incidents that may affect them
repo_note: No incident process or customer notification (see NCSC-CSP-5.3).
